bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar launches door-to-door healthcare campaign to screen 6 crore people
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 02 Sep, 2026 Bihar launches door-to-door healthcare campaign to screen 6 crore people Business To Business, Patna, 02 September 2026: Bihar has launched a major healthcare campaign aimed at taking screening, treatment and disease-prevention services directly to people's doorsteps. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the 'Jaanch evam Upchar, Chikitsa Aapke Dwar' (Testing and Treatment, Healthcare at Your Doorstep) campaign on Wednesday and flagged off awareness chariots to mark the occasion. Health Minister Nishant Kumar and Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary were also present. The campaign will run from September 2 to November 30 across Bihar's 38 districts. Under the initiative, Health Department teams will visit villages, panchayats and individual households to screen people aged between 30 years and above. The campaign will cover around 14,500 health centres across the state. The state government aims to screen around six crore people in the 30 years-and-above age group and create digital health records to facilitate the early detection and treatment of serious illnesses. The initiative will focus particularly on non-communicable and other serious diseases, including diabetes, hypertension, cancer, heart disease, respiratory and lung-related illnesses, fatty liver and tuberculosis (TB). Individuals diagnosed with a disease during the screening process will be provided medicines, medical advice and treatment, along with referrals to higher-level health facilities where necessary. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the campaign's objective is not limited to screening people. "Detailed records of individuals' illnesses and treatment histories will also be maintained and digitised. Efforts will be made to link these records with ABHA IDs, enabling the Health Department to maintain comprehensive information on people suffering from diseases such as diabetes, TB and cancer," he added. Chief Minister Choudhary said that awareness chariots would travel across districts, villages and communities to spread information about diseases and ways to prevent them. He also directed Health Department officials to ensure effective implementation of the campaign. The Bihar government has also placed special emphasis on addressing anaemia among women and girls. According to government data cited at the event, more than 63 per cent of women in Bihar suffer from anaemia. The state government plans to screen around one crore women and girls to identify and treat anaemia and other health conditions. The state government is simultaneously expanding the capacity of district hospitals to provide treatment for a wider range of diseases. The number of diseases for which treatment is available at the district level has increased from 36 to 46, while efforts are also underway to expand ICU beds and surgical facilities. According to the Chief Minister, more than 8,000 surgeries are currently performed every month in district hospitals. Recruitment of doctors and nurses is also being undertaken to strengthen healthcare services. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said that 700 nurses were appointed before Raksha Bandhan and assured that further recruitment would be carried out as required. The state government is also focusing on preparing Bihar's healthcare workforce for international opportunities. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar identifies over 8 lakh manuscripts for digitisation | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 02, 2026 Bihar identifies over 8 lakh manuscripts as govt steps up digitisation under Gyan Bharatam Mission Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Bihar government has stepped up the digitisation and preservation of manuscripts under the Centre's Gyan Bharatam Mission, with more than eight lakh manuscripts identified across all 38 districts of the state, a minister said on Wednesday. The nationwide mission aims to digitise and preserve ancient texts. In Bihar, the government is focusing on documenting rare palm-leaf and paper manuscripts held in libraries, museums and private collections. "An administrative approval for expenditure of Rs 6.23 crore was granted earlier this year to accelerate conservation and digitisation of manuscripts. More than eight lakh manuscripts have been identified across 38 districts of the state following an extensive survey," Bihar Art and Culture Minister Pramod Kumar Chandravansi told reporters. Department secretary Pranav Kumar said the exercise involves several stages, including identification, digitisation and preparation of metadata. Manuscripts found to be torn, fragile or decaying are being treated before being scanned and uploaded to a digital repository, he said. The secretary said the repository would eventually allow people in India and abroad to access the manuscripts. AI tools will also be used to transliterate scripts such as Brahmi and Kaithi into Hindi and English and prepare concise summaries of the texts. The government also announced plans to open a National School of Drama (NSD) campus in Bihar. Pranav Kumar said a site within a 20-25 km radius of Patna was being considered, subject to land availability and other requirements. Chandravansi also said a dedicated film portal had been created to provide information and services related to filmmaking in the state. So far, 862 film artists, 148 producers and 29 service providers have registered on the portal, according to a departmental statement. The Bihar Film Promotion Policy is also being implemented, with shooting permissions granted to more than 59 projects, including 46 feature films, two web series and 11 documentaries. The policy provides tiered subsidies of up to Rs 4 crore depending on the language and nature of a project. Local languages and themes are eligible for higher subsidies of up to 50 per cent, the secretary said. The minister said 411 artists had been identified under the Mukhyamantri Kalakar Pension Yojna, under which eligible artists receive Rs 3,000 a month. Scholarships and grants are also being provided to meritorious young people and selected institutions to promote art and culture in the state. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Patna High Court Directs Bihar Authorities to Provide Family Pension to Employee's Second Wife
bihar_raw_news.content: VIP MEMBER LOGIN Home Court Updates Court Updates Patna High Court Directs Bihar Authorities to Provide Family Pension to Employee’s Second Wife By Law Trend September 2, 2026 10:44 AM Facebook WhatsApp Twitter Print Pinterest The Patna High Court has overturned a state government order denying family pension to the second wife of a deceased employee, ruling that she cannot be deprived of her spousal status in her old age after decades of marriage and raising six children. Delivering the verdict on August 25, Justice Purnendu Singh set aside a February 5, 2019 decision by the chief engineer of the Flood Control and Water Resources Department in Muzaffarpur. The court held that the department had improperly dismissed the woman’s claim by ignoring a formal application her late husband had submitted decades earlier seeking official permission for their union. Administrative Rejection Overturned The matter originated after the death of the employee, identified in the judgment as a departmental clerk named Sah, who died on April 17, 2009. The petitioner subsequently applied for family pension benefits as his surviving spouse, submitting that the couple had lived together and had six children, including four daughters. State authorities rejected her claim on the grounds that the employee had failed to secure the necessary prior approval from the competent authority before contracting a second marriage. READ ALSO Non-framing of charges under section 149 of IPC would not vitiate conviction in absence of any prejudice towards the accused: SC The high court observed, however, that the employee had indeed submitted a formal application on February 28, 1982, requesting departmental permission to solemnise the marriage. Justice Singh held that the administration’s failure to consider this crucial record rendered the 2019 rejection unsustainable and contrary to Rule 23(2) of the Bihar Government Service Conduct Rules, 1976. State Objections and Legal Framework Opposing the writ petition, state counsel argued that the clerk had never obtained the mandatory sanction and that applicable service rules and government circulars disqualified the petitioner. The state asserted that personal law prohibits a Hindu man from entering into a second marriage while his first wife is alive. The state also relied on a September 6, 1996 Finance Department resolution. That directive clarified that a second wife who married an employee during the lifetime of his first wife is not entitled to a family pension, limiting eligibility only to minor children from the union until they reach the age of majority. Reviewing the regulatory framework, the court pointed out that while Rule 23(2) of the 1976 Conduct Rules restricts an employee with a living spouse from remarrying, it also empowers the government to grant permission if the marriage is permissible under personal law and valid grounds exist. Sign In What's Included Exclusive Stories Daily ePaper Access Smart Market Tools Curated Investment Ideas Ad-lite Experience Subscription Agencies Nepal floods have brought unusual fish into Bihar’s Gandak basin. Govt warns residents not to eat or sell unidentified fish amid health risks. The Bihar government has issued a health advisory after unusual-looking fish were found in flood-affected parts of the Gandak basin, with residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj being told not to eat, buy or sell such fish until their identity and safety are established. The warning comes as floodwaters from Nepal continue to flow into the Gandak river system, inundating several areas of northern Bihar. Fisheries officials said the flooding may have carried fish from rivers, ponds and other water bodies into unfamiliar locations, including low-lying areas and flooded local water bodies. The state fisheries division under the Department of Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources issued the advisory on Tuesday. Why the government has issued the warning Officials have cautioned that fish swept away by floodwaters can travel long distances and may pass through polluted water before reaching residential areas or local ponds. Such waters can contain sewage, contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants. Fish exposed to these conditions could potentially carry harmful bacteria, viruses or fungi, officials said. The department has therefore asked people to avoid consuming any fish they cannot identify with certainty. The advisory also warns residents against assuming that an unfamiliar fish is safe simply because it looks similar to a species that is commonly eaten. Until the authorities establish the identity of the fish and confirm that it is suitable for consumption, people have been advised to keep away from it. Live Events Health warning for residents The government has also asked people to remain alert for possible symptoms after eating fish caught from flood-hit areas. Anyone who develops vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or difficulty breathing after consuming such fish should seek medical attention immediately, according to the advisory. The warning applies not only to consumption but also to the purchase and sale of unidentified fish recovered from floodwaters. Nepal flood strange fish: What's the strange fish that is leading to health issues? Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most of the unusual fish being reported from the Gandak following the Nepal floods are believed to be Bagarius bagarius , commonly known as the goonch catfish . It is also locally called “Gochita”. The freshwater species is native to fast-flowing rivers in India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. It is a carnivorous fish and feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic creatures. Goonch catfish are generally found in deeper parts of rivers, particularly around rocky stretches where water currents are strong. bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 2, 2026 8:12 AM Bihar steps up flood control measures as Ganga erosion intensifies Amid the threat of flooding in Bihar’s border districts following floods in Nepal, severe erosion along the Ganga in Bhagalpur has raised concern. In Shankarpur of Kharik block, the situation remains sensitive due to the strong current and pressure of the river. Akashvani correspondent reports that severe erosion along the Ganga has washed away an old Durga temple, a Hanuman temple and around 500 metres of the Zamindari embankment in the Naugachhia block. People from the affected areas have been shifted to safer locations. Teams of the Water Resources Department are working on a war footing to control the erosion. Senior officials and engineers are present at the site and are continuously monitoring the situation. Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary said that the erosion has intensified due to an unexpected change in the course of the Ganga. He said all possible efforts are being made to check the erosion and the situation is being closely monitored. Meanwhile, a rise in the water levels of major rivers has led to flooding at several places in Saran, Vaishali, Begusarai, Buxar, Jehanabad, Nawada and Aurangabad. The administration and the Water Resources Department are maintaining close vigil in vulnerable areas.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar power minister invites investors, highlights solar plan - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 02, 2026 Bihar power minister invites investors, highlights solar plan Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Bihar Power Minister Shailesh Kumar alias Bulo Mandal on Tuesday invited national and global investors to partner in the State’s rapid economic and energy growth, assuring them of full administrative support and an enabling environment. Addressing the inaugural session of ‘Bharat Electricity 2026’ on the theme Energy Sovereignty for a Climate-Resilient Viksit Bharat, the Minister showcased Bihar’s modernised power sector. He inaugurated the Bihar Power Pavilion, highlighting the State’s strides in clean energy, storage systems, and digital grid transformation. Kumar revealed that Bihar has installed over 94 lakh smart prepaid meters, successfully reducing Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses from around 60 per cent to 11.54 per cent. He added that the State recently met a record peak demand of 9,475 MW, with projections expected to touch 19,033 MW by FY 2037. Outlining upcoming initiatives, the Minister announced a scheme to provide free 1.1 kW rooftop solar systems to 2.5 lakh Below Poverty Line (BPL) families in the coming months. Key future projects highlighted at the pavilion included a 1,200 MW Pumped Storage Plant at Nawada, major solar-plus-storage setups in Lakhisarai, and initial discussions on nuclear energy options. “Come to Bihar not merely as investors, but as our partners. Our goal is to ensure every consumer becomes energy sovereign,” Kumar stated, emphasising the need for climate-resilient infrastructure to withstand natural calamities like floods and storms. Senior officials, including Delhi Power Minister Ashish Sood and Central Electricity Authority Chairman Ghanshyam Prasad, attended the event. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Chief Minister Inaugurates Patna Flyover Phase One - RAHSTA Expo 2026
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Chief Minister Inaugurates Patna Flyover Phase One Infrastructure Transport Sep 02 2026 Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the first phase of the Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover and the two point one km Mithapur-Sipara elevated road in Patna on Friday, the Chief Minister's Office said. The works are intended to ease traffic congestion and improve connectivity to Patna railway station, Mithapur bus stand and adjacent neighbourhoods. The inauguration marked opening of the initial stretch under the broader Mithapur-Mahuli-Punpun project. The chief minister performed the ceremonial ribbon cutting and unveiled a plaque to mark the opening. According to the CMO, the Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover, including approach and service roads linking Mithapur bus stand to Mithapur roundabout via the newly constructed Karbigahiya roundabout, was constructed at a cost of Rs 2.49 billion (bn). The elevated road section from Mithapur to Sipara spans two point one km. The CMO said the roundabout is expected to reduce traffic pressure and ease commuting for rail passengers and the general public. The works form part of efforts to enhance urban mobility and optimise traffic management along the corridor. After the inauguration, the chief minister inspected the flyover and reviewed traffic arrangements on foot and by vehicle, and officials examined facilities and traffic flow systems associated with the projects. The administration said the new corridor will facilitate smoother movement and help reduce vehicular congestion on major routes. Officials also noted improved connectivity for travel towards Punpun via Mahuli. Officials inspected signage, lighting and emergency access provisions during their review. Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Road Construction Minister Kumar Shailendra and other ministers, legislators and senior officials attended the opening, and senior administrative and police officers accompanied the delegation. The state described the two projects as significant steps towards modernising the traffic system in the capital and ensuring safe and seamless commuting for citizens. Also present were the chief minister's principal secretary Deepak Kumar, road construction department secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal and Patna district magistrate Kundan Kumar among other senior officers. The largest of the three projects is an 11 Km bypass-line between Adra end and Joychandipahar in South Eastern Railway. In Gujarat, the yard remodeling project also includes two under bridges, one new RUB, an extension of a present RUB and service buildings. bihar_raw_news.title: MoU inked by Bihar -Jharkhand, Settling 25-Year Sone Water Dispute, Not Final Measure Of Success
bihar_raw_news.content: For a Sone river water-sharing dispute that has endured for nearly 25 years, signing the MoU is an important milestone—but not the final measure of success. The agreement will acquire its real significance only when its provisions translate into dependable water availability, functioning infrastructure and greater water security for communities across both States. The challenge now is to turn political consensus into administrative execution, and an inter-State settlement into a lasting public benefit. A Dispute That Spanned Decades Bihar and Jharkhand signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi on August 31 to settle their nearly 25-year-old dispute over the sharing of Sone River water. The agreement was signed in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil. Indeed, a long-running inter-State dispute over the Sone River has moved towards resolution with a formal water-sharing agreement, potentially reshaping irrigation and drinking-water access across large parts of Bihar and Jharkhand. Water Allocation Defined Under the agreement, Bihar will receive 5.75 million acre-feet (MAF) of Sone water, while Jharkhand will have a share of 2 MAF, bringing clarity to the allocation that had remained contested for years. The pact is expected to strengthen irrigation and drinking-water availability across several districts. In Bihar, these include Bhojpur, Buxar, Rohtas, Kaimur, Aurangabad, Arwal, Gaya and Patna. In Jharkhand, Palamu, Garhwa and other areas are expected to benefit. A Test of Cooperative Federalism The Centre has positioned the agreement as an example of cooperative federalism, with the Inter-State Council playing a role in addressing long-pending water disputes. The Sone settlement is among four major inter-State agreements reached this year through such efforts. From Agreement to Implementation The signing closes a prolonged chapter of disagreement, but its larger significance will depend on implementation. The real measure of the pact will be whether the agreed allocation translates into reliable water for farms, communities and drinking-water systems across both States. For millions dependent on the river, the settlement marks the beginning of that test—not its conclusion. From Paper to Pipeline The agreement settles the question of allocation; the harder task now is translating that settlement into water on the ground. Its success will depend on coordinated implementation by both States—clear mechanisms for regulating and monitoring flows, strengthening the infrastructure needed to carry the allocated water, and ensuring that irrigation and drinking-water benefits reach the districts identified under the pact. With Bihar allocated 5.75 million acre-feet and Jharkhand 2 million acre-feet, the next phase must be about measurable delivery rather than merely formal resolution. national_raw_news.content: The Government has reduced the stock holding limit for sugar dealers from 4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals, effective from the 15th of this month till the 30th of November this year. Our Correspondent reports that the new stock limit is aimed at curbing hoarding and speculative trading, protect consumer interest by ensuring adequate availability and price stability. Currently, a stock holding limit of four thousand quintals on sugar dealers across the country is effective from the 1st of the last month. Under the amended provisions, a sugar dealer shall not hold any stock for a period exceeding 30 days from the date of receipt of such stock. The sugar dealer shall also not keep sugar in stock at any time and in any place throughout the country in excess of two thousand quintals. However, the stock holding limit shall remain at four thousand quintals for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, considering the specific market requirements of the region. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the Kolkata area is sourcing sugar from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplying it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region. Therefore, the existing limit of four thousand quintals has been retained for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas. The Government has assured consumers that it is taking all necessary steps to maintain adequate availability, orderly supplies and price stability of sugar in the domestic market, while ensuring that genuine trade and distribution activities continue without disruption.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 124 Indian Forensic team begins DNA analysis to identify flash flood victims in Nepal
national_raw_news.content: A 19-member Indian forensic team has begun analysing DNA samples alongside forensic experts to assist in identifying people affected by the recent flash floods in Nepal. The Indian Embassy said that the team commenced the analysis at the Nepal Police Central Forensic Science Laboratory and the National Forensic Science Laboratory in the Khumaltar area of Kathmandu Valley. The Indian experts are working with their counterparts to speed up the processing of DNA samples collected from flood-affected areas and help establish the identities of victims and missing persons. The deployment of Indian forensic team is part of ongoing efforts to support Nepal in the aftermath of the recent flash floods, which caused significant loss of life and left several people unaccounted for. Nepal Police said 1,068 bodies have been recovered by yesterday evening, of which 400 had only partial remains, complicating the identification process. With the death toll continuing to rise following last week’s deadly floods, authorities have collected DNA samples from several unclaimed bodies to support identification efforts in the future. Chitwan district has reported the highest number of recovered bodies so far. Authorities have buried hundreds of bodies in open spaces along riverbanks after collecting DNA samples for future identification. According to Nepal Police, 4,606 people remain unaccounted for, including 583 foreigners, raising concerns that the death toll could increase further. Authorities said efforts are continuing to trace people who remain unaccounted for at various hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 91 US launches fresh strikes on IRGC targets inside Iran
national_raw_news.content: The US has begun fresh strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets inside Iran. Iranian media reported that explosions were heard in Bandar Abbas, Hormuz, Asaluyeh, Jiroft, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Chabahar, Jask, Sirik and Lavan. US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it completed the wave of strikes against Iranian military targets, which included air defence sites, mine-laying capabilities, and communications sites, among others. It said that the strikes follow recent attempted attacks by IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said that the US strikes hit a home hosting a wedding ceremony in the city of Kuhestak, resulting in the deaths of four civilians and over 50 injuries. US President Donald Trump, in a post on Truth Social, has warned that any retaliation by Iran against the very justified attack will see a stronger response by Washington. Trump also hinted that a much bigger attack against Tehran is yet to come. In response, Iran’s IRGC claimed an attack on US military barracks at Jordan’s Camp Titin. Iran’s army said it targeted US forces stationed at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa airbase. Kuwait’s army said the country’s air defences responded to attacks by “hostile drones” from Iran.

national_raw_news.title: Heavy rainfall disrupts normal life in Jharkhand 1 min ago 1
national_raw_news.content: Heavy rainfall over the past three days has disrupted normal life in Jharkhand. Rising water levels in rivers and damage to several bridges have aggravated the flood situation and affected connectivity in several parts of the state. According to IMD Ranchi, heavy rainfall in Jharkhand over the past three days has lead to a rise in the water levels of the Bhairavi, Damodar, Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers. In Ranchi, due to continuous rainfall, water has been released from the Kanke and Getalsud dams, as well as the Tenughat and Chandil dams, increasing the risk of flooding in low-lying areas. Meanwhile, several bridges and roads across the state have been damaged in the rainfall over the past three days, affecting connectivity between several villages in rural areas and their respective block and district headquarters. Lohardaga district has been among the worst affected, with several bridges damaged or washed away, impacting a large population. Connectivity has also been disrupted in Garhwa, Latehar, Ramgarh and Simdega. The Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for Simdega, West Singhbhum, Palamu and Garhwa today, while an orange alert has been issued for Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla, Khunti, Seraikela-Kharsawan and East Singhbhum. According to weather scientists, the system formed over the Bay of Bengal is expected to move through western parts of Jharkhand over the next 36 hours. Under its influence, several districts may receive heavy rainfall today, while weather conditions are likely to improve from tomorrow.
